plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49]. The Nash equilibrium bidding strategy for a first-price auction with n bidders and uniform values is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which balances winning probability against profit margin. With n=3, I should bid (2/3)*23 ≈ 15.3. This maximizes expected profit given other rational bidders follow similar strategies.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is value × (n-1)/n = value × 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitively bidding. Given my value of $18, I'll bid $12, which follows this equilibrium strategy and should maximize expected profit against similarly rational opponents.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction bid strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which for n=3 is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $39, so bidding around $26 maximizes expected profit by accounting for competition from Andy and Betty while still capturing surplus if I win.
